question: How do I reset my Duke NetID password?
reference: Go to oit.duke.edu and use the NetID Account Self-Service tool. You'll need to verify your identity, then set a new password. The new password must meet Duke's complexity requirements. If you've forgotten the security information needed for self-service, contact the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200 (or DHTS Service Desk at 919-684-2243 for Duke Health users). After resetting, you may need to update saved passwords on devices that use your NetID for wifi, mail, or VPN.

question: I'm trying to connect to the Duke VPN but it keeps failing. What should I do?
reference: The university VPN uses the Cisco AnyConnect client (or Cisco Secure Client on newer installs). To connect: open the client, enter asus-vpn.duke.edu or vpn.duke.edu as the server, enter your NetID and NetID password, then complete MFA in the Second Password / MFA Option field. Type '1' for a Duo push, enter a 6-digit Duo passcode, or touch a YubiKey. The Group should usually be left as '-Default-'. If the connection fails, confirm you have internet access outside VPN, confirm your NetID password works at oit.duke.edu, and make sure your Duo Mobile app is set up and has notifications enabled. If it still fails, contact the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200.

question: How do I set up Duo Mobile for multi-factor authentication?
reference: Multi-factor authentication is required for most Duke services. To set up Duo, go to the MFA enrollment page linked from oit.duke.edu and log in with your NetID. Add a device, typically a smartphone, and install the Duo Mobile app from the App Store or Google Play. Scan the QR code shown in the enrollment portal with the Duo app to link your device. We recommend enrolling at least one backup method, such as a second device or a YubiKey, in case your primary device is lost. After enrollment, you'll be prompted for Duo whenever you log into Duke services that require MFA.

question: I'm getting a Duo prompt on my phone but I'm not trying to log in. What does this mean?
reference: Do NOT approve the request. An unexpected Duo prompt means someone is attempting to log in with your NetID and password and they may have stolen your credentials. Tap 'Deny' in the Duo app, and if available, tap the option to report it as fraudulent. Then immediately change your NetID password using the self-service tool at oit.duke.edu. Contact the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200 (or DHTS Service Desk at 919-684-2243 for Duke Health) to report the attempted compromise. Review recent account activity if available.

question: How do I connect to eduroam wifi on my Mac?
reference: Eduroam is the recommended wifi for Duke community members and lets you also connect on other eduroam-participating campuses. To set up on macOS: go to oit.duke.edu/service/eduroam and click the JoinNow link, which downloads the SecureW2 JoinNow installer. Open the .dmg in your Downloads folder, double-click the SecureW2 JoinNow application, allow it to run if macOS warns about an internet download, then enter your Duke NetID and password when prompted. You may also be asked for your Mac's local admin password (which is different from your NetID password). The installer will configure the eduroam profile automatically. After it finishes, eduroam should appear in your wifi list and connect with your saved credentials.

question: What's the difference between Dukeblue and eduroam? Which should I use?
reference: Both are wifi networks on Duke's campus. Eduroam is the recommended choice for Duke community members because it also lets you connect at other eduroam-participating universities worldwide using your Duke NetID, and uses a configuration profile (installed via SecureW2 JoinNow) that handles authentication automatically. Dukeblue is Duke's local campus wireless and works directly with NetID credentials. For most students, faculty, and staff, eduroam is the better default. Use Dukeblue if eduroam isn't working or if you need it for setup reasons. Both require a valid Duke NetID.

question: How do I access Duke Box and what's it for?
reference: Duke Box is Duke's cloud-based storage and collaboration service, available to all members of the Duke community. Sign in at duke.box.com using your NetID and password (via Duke single sign-on). You can upload files, share folders with other Duke users or external collaborators, and access files from a browser or by installing Box Drive on your computer. Box is appropriate for most working documents; however, check Duke data classification policies before storing sensitive data such as PHI, student records, or research data subject to a data use agreement. For questions about what data is appropriate for Box, contact the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200.

question: My laptop won't print to ePrint. Where do I start troubleshooting?
reference: ePrint is Duke's campus print system. First, confirm you're connected to a Duke network (eduroam or Dukeblue) — ePrint requires you to be on the Duke network, not a hotspot or off-campus connection. Make sure the ePrint software is installed and that you've selected the correct print queue (such as ePrint_OIT for black-and-white). When you print, you'll be prompted for your NetID. Check that you have enough print funds remaining — students receive an allocation each semester, and you can add funds through the Self-Service portal if needed. If those check out and printing still fails, restart the print job, then contact the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200.

question: I'm a new employee and I haven't received my NetID yet. What do I do?
reference: New employees receive their NetID and instructions for setting an initial password during IT onboarding, usually coordinated through your department or hiring manager. If you haven't received this within a few days of your start date, contact your hiring manager or departmental IT contact first, since they often initiate the request. If that doesn't resolve it, contact the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200 with your full name, department, and start date. Do not share or guess NetIDs of others. Until you have your NetID, you won't be able to access most Duke services including email, VPN, and wifi (other than guest wifi).

question: Can I share my NetID password with a colleague who needs to access something for me while I'm out?
reference: No. Sharing your NetID password violates Duke's IT policies and the terms you agreed to when you activated your NetID. It also defeats MFA: anyone with your password and a way to receive your Duo prompts effectively becomes you, and any action they take is attributed to your account. If a colleague needs access to specific resources, the right approach is to grant them appropriate permissions through the system itself — for example, sharing a Box folder, delegating mailbox access in Outlook, or using a Sponsored Account for a non-Duke collaborator. For account-level access needs, contact the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200 to discuss the right mechanism.

question: I lost my YubiKey and I used it for Duo. How do I log in now?
reference: If you enrolled a backup Duo method (such as the Duo Mobile app on your phone or a second device), use that backup method to log in. Then, as soon as possible, log into the Duo self-service portal (linked from oit.duke.edu) and remove the lost YubiKey from your enrolled devices so it can't be used by someone who finds it. If the YubiKey was your only enrolled method, contact the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200 to verify your identity and have it removed. Replace it with a new device or YubiKey through the enrollment portal. Treat a lost YubiKey similarly to a lost ID card.

question: Is it safe to use ChatGPT for work that involves Duke student data?
reference: It depends on which version of ChatGPT and what kind of data. Duke has data security agreements covering certain AI services (such as the OpenAI models available through Duke's AI Gateway and Duke GPT), and those are appropriate for some Duke data when the data classification policy permits. The public consumer ChatGPT website is NOT covered by a Duke data agreement and should not be used with student data, PHI, or any data classified as protected or restricted. Class catalogs are public, but student names, grades, class rosters, section locations, and identifying information are not. When in doubt, check the Duke data classification policy and consult with your departmental IT contact or the OIT Service Desk at 919-684-2200 before pasting Duke data into any AI tool.
